title: PropertyVisit — a buyer-first redesign
question: Choose a direction to preview. Both use native phone navigation, real property facts, working filters, and a clear booking flow.

options.label: Material Index
options.thesis: Photography leads; precise property facts sit on a cool mineral-blue canvas.
options.viewport: Catalog title, search and city/room filters, then broad property photos with aligned price and room/area facts; two native bottom tabs.
options.risk: The mineral canvas needs strong photography or the app can feel too clinical.

raised.raise: Align price, rooms, and area consistently across every listing.
Give every property equally useful photographic space.
Give selection a clear, consistent color role.
Make the type hierarchy decisive without ornamental display type.
Keep date, time, and booking status together in viewing summaries.
Keep image proportions and comparison facts consistent.

options.label: Residential Index
options.thesis: A crisp, image-first property app with a deep-blue search header and quiet white listing rows.
options.viewport: A blue title/search region above city and room filters; white listing rows show price first, then property name and address; native tabs stay visible.
options.risk: Familiar and effective, but closer to established property apps than the other direction.

options.label: Concourse board
options.thesis: A dense, high-contrast index of properties and appointments.
options.viewport: Search over dense photo-and-fact rows, with amber used only for pending appointments.
options.risk: Weak buyer identification; density makes homes feel like departures.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and property clarity.
options.kept: Aligned comparison facts, not flap animation.

options.label: Character catalog
options.thesis: An evenly paced property roster with soft blue and lilac surfaces.
options.viewport: Native filters over equal-size property cells with clear names and facts.
options.risk: Playful merchandising weakens confidence for a major purchase.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and property clarity.
options.kept: Equal photographic attention for every property.

options.label: Garden guide
options.thesis: An optimistic green shell with saturated selection states.
options.viewport: A green catalog header and standard native filters over photo-led listings.
options.risk: The leisure-guide association is weaker than the residential context.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and property clarity.
options.kept: Selection color must communicate state, not decorate.

options.label: Type specimen
options.thesis: Strong price typography on a monochrome property index.
options.viewport: Large prices, photo rows, native filters, and a conventional tab bar.
options.risk: Bitmap character reduces legibility and feels unrelated to buying a home.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and property clarity.

options.label: Travel document
options.thesis: Appointments carry clear date, time, and persistent status.
options.viewport: Standard property navigation with compact appointment summaries and highlighted changes.
options.risk: Schedule-first emphasis makes property discovery secondary.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and clarity of the primary browsing task.
options.kept: Date, time, and status remain together.

options.label: Botanical folio
options.thesis: Consistent photographic framing makes property comparison easier.
options.viewport: Repeated photo proportions over tidy property facts with native navigation and booking controls.
options.risk: Botanical labeling and warm paper are a distraction from residential decisions.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and property clarity.
options.kept: Consistent photo scale and repeated comparison landmarks.

canonCard.label: Familiar property-app standard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional property app, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Search, filters, listing photos, prices, and native navigation.
